query: NVIDIA data center compute versus networking revenue breakdown
normalized: breakdown center compute data networking nvidia revenue

output.content:
**NVIDIA no longer reports a Data Center compute-versus-networking split in its current reporting framework.** Beginning in FY2027, it reports Data Center revenue by **Hyperscale** and **AI Clouds, Industrial & Enterprise (ACIE)** instead. [[1]]

**Last directly comparable compute/networking disclosure — Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended April 26, 2026):**

| Data Center sub-market | Revenue | Share of Data Center revenue |
|---|---:|---:|
| Compute | **$60.4bn** | **80.3%** |
| Networking | **$14.8bn** | **19.7%** |
| **Data Center total** | **$75.2bn** | **100.0%** |

NVIDIA reported Q1 FY2027 Data Center compute revenue of $60.4 billion, up 18% sequentially and 77% year over year, while networking revenue was $14.8 billion, up 35% sequentially and 199% year over year. [[2]] 
The $75.2 billion Data Center total represented 92% of NVIDIA’s $81.6 billion company revenue in that quarter. [[2]]

**Latest reported quarter — Q2 FY2027 (quarter ended July 26, 2026):** Data Center revenue was **$89.0 billion**, up 18% sequentially and 117% year over year, but NVIDIA did not provide a compute/networking revenue split under the new framework. [[3]] 
Instead, the Q2 Data Center mix was **$48.7 billion Hyperscale (54.7%)** and **$40.3 billion ACIE (45.3%)**. [[4]] 
Thus, networking’s unusually rapid growth was clear in the final legacy breakout, but investors should not infer a Q2 compute/networking split from the new customer/channel-oriented Hyperscale and ACIE categories. [[1]] [[2]]
